title: Eight A at once, T = 0.6: does the pair law add up for four pairs at r0 = 2.5?
pitch: Four horizontal A-A pairs at rest (r0 = 2.5) at centres (2.25 or 7.75, 2.25 or 7.75), so N = 8. T = 0.6, sample_dt 0.003, tracker. Cross-pair gaps are 3.0 and up; minimum separation over the run about 2.0. Pre-registered: the pairwise-additive P-0024 law (exponent 2.10) predicts the run, with residual rms per coordinate at or below 0.06 (tracker noise 0.05) as a pass. The window lies inside P-0024's (r0 in [2.5, 3.0], T <= 0.6), so a fail points at multi-body terms, not the pair law. A pass gives a crowd-8 claim.
